answer.rationale: The p99 write latency spike began 30 minutes after the release deployment, strongly implicating a code regression as the root cause. Memory_b1 demonstrates that rolling back a problematic release previously resolved a similar production incident (checkout error spike) with no customer impact, establishing rollback as a proven, low-risk remediation. Memory_b2, while confirming regional failover can restore latency, is rejected here because failover during peak write traffic risks data inconsistency and write loss. Rollback to the known-stable prior build directly addresses the likely root cause while preserving all customer writes. Capacity addition or circuit breakers would not remediate a code-level issue.
